name: Spain
headline_status: Cannabis is not legal in Spain, but private use is not a crime and public use draws administrative fines; a hospital-only medical programme was created in October 2025.
summary: Possessing drugs for personal use is not a crime under Spain's Penal Code, but carrying or using cannabis in public is an administrative offence with fines starting at €601. Private non-profit cannabis associations operate in a legal grey area and have faced police raids and adverse court rulings. In October 2025 the government approved Royal Decree 903/2025, letting specialist doctors prescribe standardised cannabis preparations dispensed by hospital pharmacies, and the first products were registered in July 2026.

possession_limit.value: Private possession for personal use is not a crime; public possession is an administrative offence. Amounts above roughly 100 g of cannabis or 25 g of hashish can be treated as trafficking.

public_use.value: Public possession or use is fined under Organic Law 4/2015 from €601 up to €30,000; a first small offence usually draws the €601 minimum, which can be halved for prompt payment.

penalties.value: Trafficking without aggravating factors carries 3 to 6 years in prison; growing plants visible to the public can be fined.

retail_sales.value: No legal retail. Private non-profit cannabis associations operate in a legal grey area and have been raided and ruled against by courts, notably in Catalonia.

medical_since.value: Royal Decree 903/2025, approved by the Council of Ministers on 7 October 2025.

medical_program.value: Specialist doctors may prescribe standardised cannabis preparations, with documented justification, when other treatments have failed (e.g. MS spasticity, refractory epilepsy, chemotherapy nausea, refractory chronic pain); hospital pharmacies prepare and dispense them.

regulator.value: Spanish Agency of Medicines and Medical Devices (AEMPS), which keeps the registry of standardised cannabis preparations.

tourists.value: Visitors face the same public-use fines as residents. Some cannabis associations admit tourists with ID and a local address, but many are referral-only and all operate in a legal grey area.

timeline.event: Organic Law 4/2015 sets administrative fines for public drug possession and use
Council of Ministers approves Royal Decree 903/2025 on medical cannabis
First standardised cannabis preparations (Curaleaf CAN-1 and CAN-2) registered with AEMPS

faq.a: No, but using it in private is not a crime. Possessing or using cannabis in public brings a fine from €601.

faq.q: Can tourists join cannabis clubs in Spain?
faq.a: Some associations accept visitors with ID and a local address, but many are referral-only, and clubs operate in a legal grey area.

faq.q: Is medical cannabis legal in Spain?
faq.a: Yes, since Royal Decree 903/2025. Specialists can prescribe standardised preparations that are dispensed only by hospital pharmacies.
